sections.title: About 1Password
paras: At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

As the Senior Director, Implementation, you’ll report to the Vice President, Customer Success and set the strategic and operational direction for 1Password’s implementation and professional services function. You’ll lead a team responsible for helping customers across Small and Medium-sized Businesses (SMB), Commercial, and Enterprise segments adopt 1Password successfully, improve time to value, and achieve measurable outcomes.

sections.title: How we’re using AI today
paras: Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.
This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

sections.title: What we're looking for:
bullets: Bring 10+ years of experience in professional services, customer onboarding, or implementation, including at least 5 years in a leadership role, with experience in cybersecurity and Software as a Service (SaaS) environments.
Demonstrate a strong background in technical implementations, systems, infrastructure, and integrations for complex customers.
Apply experience from implementation, professional services, solutions architecture, or technical account management environments.
Scale onboarding and implementation programs across SMB, Commercial, and Enterprise customer segments.
Build capacity-planning models and use utilization, delivery performance, and other Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to guide decisions.
Combine strategic thinking with a willingness to engage directly in complex customer situations, team challenges, and operational details.
Influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners through clear communication, sound judgment, data, and a strong understanding of customer and business needs.

sections.title: What you can expect:
paras: USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $192,000 USD and $264,000 USD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $182,000 CAD and $250,000 CAD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Our culture
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone . Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.
bullets: Define and execute the strategic vision for implementation and professional services, including the launch and evolution of scalable services offerings.
Lead, coach, and grow a cross-functional team of Solutions Architects, Onboarding Specialists, Project Managers, and Implementation Specialists.
Establish scalable playbooks, frameworks, and processes that improve onboarding, implementation quality, customer adoption, and time to value.
Partner with Sales, Customer Success, Product, Marketing, and Operations to create effective transitions from pre-sale activities through customer implementation.
Oversee implementation delivery across customer segments, ensuring projects meet scope, timeline, quality, and outcome expectations.
Use data and reporting to monitor project health, capacity, utilization, customer outcomes, and opportunities for improvement.
Serve as an escalation point for complex implementation challenges while leading change initiatives that strengthen team effectiveness and customer results.

sections.title: The Role
paras: We're looking for a Senior Enterprise Customer Success Manager to own the full customer lifecycle for our most strategic accounts, including: onboarding, implementation, adoption, expansion, and renewal.

Accord helps revenue organizations transform how they execute the customer journey. This role is a true partner to revenue leadership at our customers: CROs, VPs of Sales, RevOps, and Sales Enablement.

In this key role, you will define how this function operates as much as you execute it. You'll personally lead 8-12+ week transformational implementations and advise a portfolio of 10-15 matrixed enterprise accounts, with 35-50+ active stakeholders per account spanning rev ops, sales leadership, enablement, and frontline reps.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own the full customer journey: Lead onboarding, hands-on implementation (typically 8-12+ weeks of change management), and adoption for enterprise customers from kickoff to go-live.
Multi-thread complex organizations: Build and maintain relationships across 35-50+ stakeholders per account, executive sponsors, champions, technical evaluators, and end users.
Drive measurable outcomes: Translate Accord adoption into quantified revenue impact, shorter sales cycle, higher win rates, methodology adherence, rep ramp time, etc.
Own renewals and expansion: Lead renewal forecasting, negotiation, and close. Identify and sequence expansion opportunities across our product suite.
Be a strategic advisor: Coach revenue leaders through process change, methodology adoption, and organizational alignment.
Build the foundation: Contribute to scalable processes, playbooks, and customer education as we grow the CS function. Bring structure to ambiguity.
Partner cross-functionally: Collaborate with Sales, Product, and Marketing and provide feedback that informs product roadmap and GTM strategy.
Champion our customers internally: Represent customer needs directly to founders, product leadership, shaping our roadmap and GTM strategy.

sections.title: Who You Are
bullets: Experienced operator: 5+ years as an operator in Customer Success, Account Management, or Implementation at a B2B SaaS company, managing mid-market and Enterprise accounts. Experience in sales tools/technology, or working closely with sales leaders, is a plus.

Strategic Advisor: Senior-level presence with proven influence at the C-suite on customer accounts. Rigorous and structured in communication. You know what each stakeholder values, you can map who actually makes purchasing decisions in a complex buying committee, and you can hold your own with a CRO.
Implementation depth: Lead multi-week transformational implementations across workstreams, dependencies, and stakeholders.
Product depth: You know your current product cold: features, gaps, edge cases, strategic rationale and can articulate where it creates value and where it falls short.

Consultative: You've led change management and advised customers on process, methodology, and adoption. You have a recent example of redesigning a customer's workflow or coaching them through organizational change.
Commercially minded: Owned NDR/GRR targets directly. Comfortable leading renewal forecasting and negotiation.

Value-driven communicator: Frame every customer interaction around measurable business outcomes: ROI, adoption metrics, revenue impact, not just operational satisfaction or NPS. Bring data into renewal and expansion conversations as a default.

ashby:brightwheel:611f1e11-d266-49cc-a4a.summary: Early education is one of the most important determinants of childhood outcomes, a critical support for working families, and a $175B market that remains underserved by modern technology. Brightwheel is the largest, fastest growing, and most loved platform in early ed, trusted by millions of educators and families every day. We are a three-time Cloud 100 company , backed by top investors including Addition, Bessemer, Emerson Collective, Lowercase Capital, Notable Capital, and Mark Cuban.

sections.title: Our Team
paras: Our team is passionate, talented, and customer-focused. We embody our Leadership Principles in our work and culture. We are a distributed team with remote employees across every US time zone, as well as select offices in the US and internationally.

sections.title: Who You Are
paras: You are an AI-native product leader and builder who combines world-class product taste, deep customer empathy, and high standards with the drive to build something new, and you want that something to matter. You create clarity in ambiguous spaces, turn a first product line into a real business, and lead by example in how modern products get built. You care about the teacher who opens the app at 7:25 with nine toddlers arriving, the parent who wants to know their child is learning, and the state official who has to show what a year of funding bought. You move with the urgency and ownership of a founder.

sections.title: You will succeed in this role if you are
bullets: Here for the mission. You want the outcome measured in what children learn and what teachers can do, and you know that a business that grows is how that outcome reaches millions of children instead of thousands.
Focused on customer and business impact. You care about creating real value for families and educators, and about proving a business that can grow into something meaningful for brightwheel.
A practitioner-builder. You do not lead from a distance. You use AI and modern tooling in your own work to build, prototype, and learn, and to show what great looks like.

sections.title: What You'll Do
paras: The years before kindergarten shape everything that comes after, and early education is where the gap between children first opens. brightwheel sits at the center of it, trusted by tens of thousands of schools and millions of families, with the distribution and profitable core most founders never get to start with. Our education business is where that trust turns into outcomes: curriculum that gives a teacher a plan for the day, assessments that show a parent how their child is growing, and professional development that helps teachers get better at one of the hardest and least supported jobs in education. States and districts fund these years, set the standards, and need to see results against them. Entire companies exist to do just one of these pieces. None of them also runs the school.

The opportunity now is to make education brightwheel's second core business, ten times its current size, and to put a real curriculum, a real measure of growth, and real training in front of children, teachers and families who have never had them: new segments, from states and districts to the smallest programs; new models, from digital subscriptions to multi-year contracts; and products that improve what children learn, on top of running the programs that teach them.

You will lead that work. You will take education from early traction to product-market fit in segment after segment, building with your own hands and with AI, and proving both the product and the business behind it. The mission reaches more children only if the business grows.

ashby:checkout.com:7a6b550a-f67c-4691-96.summary:
We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.

We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and…

sections.title: How you’ll make an impact
bullets: Hire, onboard, coach, and develop a high-performing account management team. Set clear expectations, provide actionable feedback, and create development plans that help people build skills and progress in their careers.
Build a culture of ownership, collaboration, and high performance. Recognize strong execution, address performance gaps promptly, and create an environment where people learn from one another.

Own the team’s commercial performance and execution against portfolio growth and retention objectives. Translate regional priorities into clear individual goals, account plans, and quarterly priorities.

Establish a disciplined operating rhythm across one-to-ones, account and opportunity reviews, forecasting, and performance reviews. Use data to distinguish underlying portfolio trends from growth driven by the team’s actions.
Coach the team to understand merchant business models, priorities, and payment performance, and translate those insights into compelling account development plans and measurable customer outcomes.

Develop a qualified expansion pipeline across share of wallet, new products, payment methods, and geographic expansion. Hold the team accountable for progressing opportunities through to adoption and realized revenue.
Guide commercial negotiations and retention strategies, helping account managers articulate value, build sound business cases, and balance merchant needs with sustainable commercial outcomes.

Act as a leadership escalation point for important merchant relationships, risks, and challenges. Join key business reviews and negotiations where your involvement can strengthen relationships or unlock progress.

sections.title: What we’re looking for
bullets: A strong track record in B2B account management or a related revenue-owning commercial function, ideally in payments, fintech, or another complex technology business.

Demonstrated leadership capability, including coaching, mentoring, setting high standards, and helping colleagues improve their commercial effectiveness. Experience managing direct reports is valuable, alongside evidence of developing others and taking accountability for shared outcomes.
A record of delivering revenue growth and retention, with the ability to translate successful commercial approaches into repeatable practices that improve team performance.
A hands-on coaching style and the ability to develop consultative commercial skills, including account planning, opportunity qualification, negotiation, and executive engagement.
Strong commercial and analytical judgment. You can interpret portfolio performance, build credible forecasts, identify the drivers behind results, and translate insight into action.
Experience managing a broad portfolio through clear prioritization, repeatable processes, and differentiated merchant engagement.

ashby:keycard-labs:d3427698-ca1b-47fc-b7.summary: At Keycard, we're building identity and access infrastructure for the agent-native era, where software isn't static but a dynamic, constantly changing system of AI agents working on behalf of people and businesses. Keycard gives every agent a verified identity and issues short-lived, task-scoped credentials at runtime, so agents can only do what they were asked to do, and every action is fully auditable. We're backed by a16z, Boldstart, and Acrew, and our founding team built and scaled Snyk, Auth0, HashiCorp, and Heroku.

sections.title: The role
paras: We're hiring a Product Manager to own how teams evaluate Keycard, and the developer experience they meet when they do.

Keycard is a control plane for agents: identity, credential exchange, delegation, policy, and audit. Every customer starts with an evaluation, and today a field engineer runs each one by hand: setup, first credential exchange, integration questions. Your job is to turn that walkthrough into product, so an evaluation can run well without us in the room.

You'll define what a successful evaluation looks like for an agent-identity product, instrument the journey so we can see where evaluators stall, then work with engineering to fix the worst spots. Sometimes the fix is a feature, more often it's a better quickstart, a template repo, an error message that says what to do next, or a docs page that assumed too much context.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Own the evaluation journey end to end, from first touch through first credential exchange to a production decision, including how each stage is defined and measured.
Set the evaluation milestones and metrics that product, engineering, and go-to-market all report against.
Own the developer experience an evaluation runs on: SDK quickstarts, CLI onboarding, console setup, docs, and template repos.
Drive time-to-first-credential-exchange down, and be the voice of developer ergonomics in engineering's API and CLI design discussions.
Turn what field engineering does by hand into self-guided paths: eval guides, reference architectures, in-product guidance. Run experiments and cut the ones that don't work.
Work with DevRel and marketing on how evaluations start, and with sales and field engineering on when a self-guided eval needs a human in the room.

sections.title: What we're looking for
bullets: You've been a PM on a developer product where evaluation and adoption were your numbers (dev tools, infrastructure, API platforms, or security).

Technical enough to be credible with engineers. You can read an SDK quickstart and see where a developer would bounce, follow an API design discussion, and pull your own numbers in SQL or an analytics tool.
You have taste in developer experience. You can articulate why one CLI feels good and another doesn't, and you notice error messages, defaults, and docs structure the way a designer notices spacing.
You build with AI tools yourself and follow the agent ecosystem closely enough to have real opinions about it.
You start from instrumentation. If the data you need doesn't exist, you get it added before forming theories about where evaluations drop off.
Comfortable in a category with no playbook. Agent identity is new, and a lot of this job is deciding which questions are worth answering.
You write clearly. Much of this role's output is docs, problem statements, and experiment readouts that other people act on.

sections.title: Strong candidates may also have
bullets: An engineering background before product; you've shipped code and understand what you're asking engineers to do.
Experience productizing a high-touch motion: turning field playbooks, POC guides, or solutions-engineering work into product.
Familiarity with identity/auth concepts (OAuth, OIDC, token exchange, delegation) or agent protocols (MCP, A2A).
Experience with growth tooling: product analytics, experimentation frameworks, lifecycle messaging.
Docs, quickstarts, or templates you shipped that developers actually used.

Custody and control models. Develop a strong product point of view across custodial, non-custodial, embedded, and hybrid wallet architectures—and make those choices understandable and useful to customers.

Enterprise customers. Work directly with fintechs, payment companies, financial institutions, marketplaces, and global businesses to understand how they hold and manage money today and where existing infrastructure falls short.

sections.title: Role Description
paras: As we scale our product surface area, we’re looking for Product Managers who are excited to own a variety of high-impact products, and drive outsized outcomes in hard-to-solve and ambiguous problem spaces. This is a role designed for builders who thrive in ambiguity, love solving complex user and workflow problems, and take full ownership of outcomes - from defining the problem space to shipping, scaling, and driving real customer and business impact.

As a Product Manager, you will be accountable for setting the vision, strategy, and end-to-end execution of one or more core product areas. This is not a “manage the roadmap” role—it’s a “make it successful” role. You’ll develop a deep understanding of users, their day-to-day workflows, and the broader ecosystem they operate in. You’ll identify the highest-leverage problems to solve and turn messy, real-world complexity into simple, scalable experiences. You will hold the standard on quality, and not rest until your product is creating the level of impact in the field that you expect.

You’ll work closely with design, engineering, customer-facing teams, and other product managers. You will lead product discovery, define clear requirements, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and push products from 0→1 and from 1→scale with urgency and clarity. This is a highly cross-functional and user-centered role—ideal for someone who loves building foundational experiences that make complex work feel effortless.

greenhouse:altanaai:8004488003.summary: Altana is the network for trusted trade. Our AI-powered product network empowers governments and businesses to build a more resilient and secure global economy while keeping trade flowing.

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: The rules of global trade are being rewritten in real time.

Supply chain transparency requirements are being rewritten; Forced labor enforcement, semiconductor export controls, tariff volatility, secure procurement for defense, allied coordination on economic security all require a new paradigm. Governments around the world are being asked to do something they've never been equipped to do: understand, monitor, and act on the full depth of global commerce, not just the edge of it. To do so they need a deep understanding of the entire production history and to collaborate with the private sector in new ways to ensure compliant trade is facilitated, while questionable activity is identified.

The tools haven't kept pace with the mandate. Customs agencies still orient around transactions and rely on paper-based trusted trader audits, defense resilience was built for a different era of acquisition and slower innovation, and agencies don’t have the tooling nor data to do fact based policy research. The result is a widening gap between what governments need to know and what they can actually see — a gap that bad actors exploit, that allies can't easily close together, and that legitimate traders pay for in delays, uncertainty, and compliance overhead.

sections.title: Redefine What Governments Can See
bullets: Own the product vision for Altana’s three public sector product areas;
Customs and Border Management For Goods – modern tooling to collaborate with importers, understand trade, and enforce policy decisions at the border
Defense resilience and acquisition – defining a new era of defense procurement to foster innovation while maintaining secure and compliant supply chains
Economic Security and Policy – helping agencies analyze supply chain information to influence effective policy
Engage in how Altana is deployed to governments to meet them where they need us across their varied geographies, security and compliance boundaries.
Ensure a unified platform and architecture to meet the needs of multiple governments.
Work in collaboration with our other product areas to define and deliver our core mission sets in ways that work for public sector users.

sections.title: Modernize Customs and Border Management For Goods
bullets: Help government customers move beyond transaction oriented, repetitive work, and adversarial sampling. Build an agent native intelligence layer that lets border authorities collaborate, review and enforce policies with modern ML and AI.
Build automated validation tools that close the "Tax Gap" — catching duty evasion, misdeclared origin, and undervaluation without slowing the flow of legitimate commerce.

Own the integration and user workflow layer: how do we coexist with government systems and user flows to bridge the world to a new future. Integrate to make Altana feel like a native capability, not another integration project.

sections.title: Power Economic Security and Policy
bullets: Define a new product capability around economic security — giving government users the analytical tools to understand supply chain concentration, map strategic dependencies, model the impact of tariff and export control policy, and coordinate with allied governments on shared risk.

Build the "Policy Workbench" that allows trade analysts, national security staff, and senior policymakers to move from raw supply chain data to defensible, evidence-based conclusions — about a sector, a country, a company, or a critical input.

Work across the U.S. interagency and with Altana's international government customers to ensure the platform supports the full spectrum of economic security missions — from forced labor enforcement to critical mineral mapping to allied supply chain coordination.
Manage a fused data environment that combines Altana’s unparalleled supply chain graph, and enables integration with confidential customer data to support policy analyses.

sections.title: ABOUT THE JOB:

The Software Product Manager for ArsenalOS will own multiple Factory-touching platforms: software that enables stakeholders such as production managers, manufacturing engineers across disciplines, and automation and controls engineers to map the physical world to a digital one (its locations, work centers, stationed tools, assets, and more) and to execute workflows at the speed we require. These platforms sit within ArsenalOS Connected Factory and will start by unifying how locations, work centers, tools, and assets are modeled across the warehouse management system (WMS), manufacturing execution system (MES), and asset management system (AMS), along with multiple different types of sensor systems, into a seamless operating environment, replacing manual processes with purpose-built systems designed for how Anduril actually builds.

You will build this product from the ground up, from vision through MVP to scaled adoption. You must be able to zoom all the way in to improve how a single user stands up a station or commissions a smart tool, sensor, tester, controller, etc., and zoom all the way out to design the systems, data models, and integrations that connect all manufacturing systems. At Anduril's build rate, every gap between the digital model of the line and its physical reality is where production quietly slows down, and closing that gap is the whole job.

sections.title: WHAT YOU'LL DO:
bullets: Define and own the product strategy and roadmap for the Forge Factory, with a clear point of view on the what, why, and why now.
Build Forge Factory from the ground up: define the vision, scope the MVP, ship it, and iterate based on real user feedback and business outcomes.
Partner with manufacturing, reliability, and product operations to define and deliver the software that connects their workflows into one coherent operating environment.
Define the integration strategy between manufacturing systems and adjacent platforms (MES, ERP, AMS & WMS), ensuring the right data flows to the right people at the right time.

Leverage AI and modern tooling to accelerate product development, from prototyping and requirements generation to building intelligent workflows that surface insights and reduce manual decision-making.

Establish metrics and feedback loops that tie product work to measurable business outcomes, e.g., time to stand up or reconfigure a production line, line changeover time, asset uptime and utilization, and reduction in manual reconciliation between Forge and the ERP.
Own prioritization, scope, tradeoff decisions, release planning, and execution quality across a cross-functional engineering team.
Drive adoption so business teams and external partners actually use what you build, and spend less time fighting software and more time ensuring hardware excellence.

Strong domain knowledge in complex operational environments where many different personas with distinct roles and requirements must be orchestrated.

Demonstrated ability to leverage AI/ML and modern tooling to accelerate product development, from rapid prototyping to intelligent product features.
You've owned a product end-to-end and can point to the business outcome it drove, not just that it shipped, but what it changed.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly to operators, engineers, business leaders, and executive stakeholders.

You will sit between the business and technology teams, working with brand, marketing operations, creative and agency stakeholders, delivery leads, engineering squads and Adobe’s product teams. Adobe innovation: Keep up with where Adobe is heading (AEM as a Cloud Service, AEM Assets, Adobe Express, Workfront and generative AI such as Adobe Firefly) and spot where new capabilities can add real business value.
Solution options: Weigh configure vs. customize vs. buy, leaning on out-of-the-box Adobe capabilities where they meet the need and keep long-term cost down.

Business partnership: Act as the main link between business stakeholders, delivery teams and Adobe, run discovery sessions and workshops with marketers, agencies, marketing operations and MLR reviewers, and build consensus when priorities compete across brands, markets and functions.
Communication: Share the roadmap, priorities, release plans, status, risks and trade-offs clearly with every audience, including senior leadership.

Backlog ownership: Own and groom the product backlog in Jira, prioritize epics and features by value against effort, risk and dependencies, and write clear epics and user stories with business context and acceptance criteria.
Integrations: Partner with architects on integrations between AEM and connected systems such as Veeva Vault PromoMats, marketing automation, CRM, analytics and agency tools.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Search is being rebuilt around AI. People increasingly get answers from AI instead of a list of links, agents run dozens of searches to answer a single question, and more than half of the traffic reaching sites on Cloudflare is now automated . Search is shifting from a destination to a utility, and Cloudflare is building the search layer for this agentic Internet.

Agentic Search at Cloudflare gives agents everything they need to find information, whether it lives in a customer’s own data or on the open web. It spans two products: AI Search for internal data, and Web Search API for the open web.

AI Search (internal data), now generally available , is the search primitive for applications and agents . It is a fully managed indexing and retrieval pipeline built on Workers AI , Vectorize , R2 , and Browser Run . Developers connect a website or R2 bucket, or upload their own files, and query them with natural language through a Workers binding, REST API, or MCP server. Under the hood: continuous indexing, hybrid vector and keyword retrieval, reranking, metadata filtering, native multimodal (image) embeddings, and OCR for scanned documents. We use it to power search on our own blog and developer docs.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Talk directly with developers, AI companies, publishers, and customers every day.
Own the strategy, roadmap, and execution for Agentic Search (AI Search and Web Search API), from ingestion and indexing through retrieval, ranking, and answer generation.
Define and measure what “good search” means, including relevance, freshness, latency, and cost, and build the evals that improve it with every release.
Scale AI Search for the workloads that matter most, like multi-tenant platforms, enterprise agents, and website search, with support for billions of documents, rich media, and built-in observability.
Take Web Search API and shape what comes next: provider partnerships, search and page extraction in one call, blending web and private data,
Own pricing and packaging, and make our products first-class for agents through MCP, agent-friendly APIs, and templates like NLWeb .
Partner with engineering, ML, and product teams across Workers AI , Vectorize , AI Gateway , Browser Run , and AI Crawl Control , as well as Marketing, DevRel, BD, Sales, and Support.
Represent Cloudflare at conferences, community events, and customer and partner meetings.

bullets: Proven experience as a PM, EM, or founder shipping search, information retrieval, data infrastructure, or developer platform products. You’ve led teams to ship before and can point to impact.

Deep understanding of how search works end to end: crawling, indexing, chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector), query rewriting, reranking, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). You understand the tradeoffs between relevance, freshness, latency, and cost.
Experience defining and measuring search quality, including offline evals, relevance judgments, metrics like recall, MRR, and NDCG, and online experimentation.
Fluency in the modern AI ecosystem: LLMs, text and multimodal embedding models, agents, tool calling, and MCP. You’ve built with them yourself and know where they break.

Hands-on ability to write code and use AI and the Internet to learn new things fast. You’ve built a RAG pipeline or an agent that searches the web, and you have opinions about what made it good or bad.
Deep empathy for developers and understanding of their workflows, pain points, and how they adopt new tools and platforms.

Understanding of the web publishing ecosystem: crawlers, bots, SEO and answer engine optimization (AEO), and the changing economics of AI search for content creators. Comfortable working where technology, business, and policy meet.
Experience with usage-based pricing, two-sided marketplaces, or partner and business development relationships, including build-vs-partner decisions, is a plus.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

sections.title: The role
paras: Okta enables universal, secure access to technology for every user and organization. Okta Customer Identity (OCI) is the identity platform behind that promise for the applications our customers build for their own customers: the login, MFA, and account management layer for millions of end users across B2B, B2B2C and B2C products. OCI sits alongside Okta Workforce Identity (OWI) as one of the two halves of the Okta platform.

We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to grow OCI's footprint inside our existing enterprise base and to incubate the next generation of platform capabilities. This is a builder's role. You'll spend a good chunk of your time in true zero-to-one territory: sizing a raw opportunity, proving it out with a design partner or two, and turning it into a capability that ships and gets adopted. You'll spend the rest of it as the connective tissue across engineering, design, research, and go-to-market, making sure those bets land in the field.

sections.title: What you will own
bullets: New Capability Incubation: Own the pipeline of zero-to-one bets on the Okta’s Okta Customer Identity platform, from a rough problem statement through a validated design and a shipped v1. You'll decide what's worth building before anyone asks engineering to build it.

Platform Growth: Drive the product side of Okta Customer Identity platform expansion into our existing enterprise base. You'll turn a hypothesis about why they haven't adopted the Okta Customer Identity platform into product changes that remove the reason.

Cross-functional Delivery: Be the person engineering, design, research, and go-to-market call when a new Okta Customer Identity platform capability needs a decision. You'll write the specs, run the reviews, and keep a dozen loosely connected workstreams moving toward the same launch.

sections.title: A day in the life
paras: Your day splits between zero-to-one thinking and shipping discipline. You might start the morning studying churn or expansion data for a segment we don't serve well yet, trying to figure out whether the gap is a feature gap or a positioning gap. An hour later you're on a call with a design partner customer, walking through a rough prototype and taking notes on what confused them.

By midday you're in execution mode: reviewing a spec with your engineering lead, debating whether a capability needs its own data model or can extend an existing one, and pushing back on scope that's grown past what the opportunity actually justifies. You write plainly. Your specs read like an explanation to a smart colleague, not a wish list.

In the afternoon you sync with go-to-market and your PMM partner on how a capability in progress should be positioned once it ships, and you flag anything that changes the pitch. You close the day presenting to a customer or prospect, walking them through what's shipped and what's coming on the roadmap.

bullets: Identify, size, and validate new zero-to-one opportunities on the Okta Customer Identity platform, using customer conversations, usage data, and market signals rather than internal opinion alone.
Define and execute a roadmap that balances new capability bets against platform reliability, security hardening, and performance
Write clear, detailed specs and requirements that give engineering and design unambiguous direction, especially in areas with no existing playbook.
